title: Routing provenance normalization + light per-hop signal facade
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Routing decisions (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variant) currently emit heterogeneous artifacts across the runtime, console, and dedicated plane. Different teams store per-hop signals in different schemas (proto, json blob, ad-hoc spans), making cross-correlation expensive and causing high cardinality storage costs. We need a normalized, lightweight ‘signal facade’ that captures an ordered per-hop summary plus optional deep-capture links for sampled flows. Goals: 1) produce a compact canonical routing event per request that reconciles region/tier/variant choices and their reasoning; 2) attach micro-metrics per-hop (latency_ms, scheduling_delay_ms, variant_score, cost_estimate_usd) in a fixed schema; 3) provide a sample-link for sampled full-traces/artifacts (KV snapshots, full policy state) stored separately; 4) keep per-request event < 2KB by default and support sampled full-capture for debugging; 5) provide mapping for Console and billing pipelines so SLOs and cost attribution can consume the same event stream.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical routing_provenance_v1 event is emitted for >= 95% of requests in hosted and dedicated environments
Default event payload size median < 1.2KB; 99th percentile < 2KB unless sampled
Per-hop condensed fields present: hop_index, region, tier, model_variant, latency_ms, scheduling_delay_ms, token_estimate, fallback_reason (if any)
Sampled full-capture link exists and resolves to a secure artifact (S3 pre-signed / internal store) for sampled flows
Console shows per-route aggregated metrics derived from the new canonical events (latency distribution by hop, fallback rate by region)
technical_design: Design overview: introduce a canonical JSON envelope (routing_provenance_v1) emitted synchronously at request completion and once for retries/fallbacks. The envelope contains: request_id, timestamp, route_summary (final region/tier/variant), hops[] where each hop is a fixed tuple of string/int primitives (hop_index, region, tier, variant, latency_ms, scheduling_delay_ms, token_estimate, fallback_flag, fallback_reason_code), and optional sampled_artifact_ref. To avoid cardinality explosions, we normalize region/tier/variant identifiers to short tokens (R:us-east-1 -> r1, T:premium -> t2) with a server-side lookup table managed by the control-plane. The client/routing runtime will emit the compact form by default; a sampling controller (configurable per-customer/route) will attach sampled_artifact_ref for 0.1% flows or higher during incident drills.
schema_notes:
- Use stable flat keys, avoid nested maps where possible; hops is an array of compact objects (but still JSON).
- Fields are typed but emitted as strings for compatibility with existing log store parsers.
- Maintain a version field to allow migration to v2 later.
- Provide a translator utility in infra repo to expand compact ids for Console/backfill jobs.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Tradeoffs: embedding micro-metrics in the routing envelope increases write volume to our event bus, however the compact canonical form is much smaller than existing ad-hoc debug captures. Sampling is needed to keep storage costs reasonable for deep-capture. Risks: mismatched normalization tables between control-plane and legacy consumers could lead to misinterpretation — mitigation: include human-readable expansions in a compact mapping service and run a two-week parallelization period where both compact and verbose forms are emitted.
instrumentation_plan:
1) Add emission point in router::decision_path at request completion (ENG runtime). 2) Add compact id mapper to control-plane sync CI so runtimes fetch latest token map. 3) Route-specific sampling config stored in Console config API. 4) New consumer in observability pipeline that validates schema, computes per-hop aggregates, and forwards metrics to metrics infra (Prometheus/Traces -> Tempo) and cost pipelines.
Links: design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Routing+Provenance+Normalization, proposal PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2142
implementation_steps: Spike: runtime prototype that emits compact routing_provenance_v1 events (ENG-21867-spike) - 2d
Control-plane: token map service + endpoints for runtimes - 3d
Runtime: integrate emission, sampling config, and fallback tagging - 5d
Observability: validator consumer and metrics bridge (console panels) - 4d
Backfill: one-week parallel verbose+compact emission and monitor mismatches - 7d
qa_and_rollout: Staged rollout: - Canary in staging -> small subset of hosted region -> Dedicated beta customers with opt-in -> full prod. QA: synthetic workload that induces region/tier fallbacks and simulated slow scheduling to validate hop metrics. Set temporary increased sampling (1%) for first 48h of prod to gather artifacts. Monitor: event size, fallback rate, mismatch errors, and Console panel correctness.
